items.label: 1A
items.claim: In NCBI's Genetic Testing Registry, the NovaSeq 6000 is named in 130 clinical test records and the NovaSeq X in only 12, about 11 to 1, as of 12 Oct 2026.
items.detail: Live esearch on db=gtr gave Count=130 for "NovaSeq 6000" and Count=12 for "NovaSeq X". A 'NovaSeq X Plus' search returns only 4 IDs (593064, 593063, 569955, 501985). Registry records are lab self-reports that are rarely edited, so the ratio shows how many labs have declared a conversion, not how much volume has moved. The 130 is a floor, because the broad term 'NovaSeq' returns 404 records, and the tail of clinical tests still declaring the 6000 is large.
items.why_new: Known list only has the 11x ratio as a lead (F952); this adds the term-level counts, the broader 404 count and the 4-record X Plus count.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Mayo Clinic Laboratories alone holds 104 of the 130 GTR NovaSeq 6000 records (80%), so the registry's 6000 tail is mostly one large reference lab.
items.detail: esearch for "NovaSeq 6000" AND "Mayo Clinic Laboratories" returned 104; 104/130 = 80%. Records I opened were current: hereditary renal cancer panel (updated 2026-05-18), Ehlers-Danlos panel (2026-04-10), SEPTIN9 and muscular dystrophy panels (2025-09-16). None of the Mayo records I opened names the X. Mayo is one of the largest US clinical reference labs, and it is still declaring the 6000 on tests refreshed in 2025-26.
items.why_new: F953 covered one Mayo record; this quantifies Mayo's share (104 of 130) and shows several current versions.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Mayo Clinic Laboratories reviewed and re-versioned its 6000-labelled tests repeatedly through 2022-2026 without switching to the X.
items.detail: The Ehlers-Danlos record has 6 versions: registered 2022-12-15, then updates on 2023-04-06, 2024-04-08, 2025-04-04, 2025-09-16 and 2026-04-10. The muscular dystrophy panel was updated 2025-04-01 and 2025-09-16, and the renal cancer panel 2024-04-15 and 2026-05-18. The instrument field stayed 'Illumina NovaSeq 6000' through every revision I could see, so the lab had many chances to change it and did not. This fits the regulated or validated clinical tail, but the field may lag the lab's actual instruments.
items.why_new: Adds a dated version history showing repeated re-attestation of the 6000 by a major clinical lab.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Tempus (xT) declares the NovaSeq 6000 for its flagship tissue test in GTR, reviewed Nov 2025.
items.detail: Tempus xT, record GTR000613444.1 (Tempus AI - RTP), lists 'Novaseq 6000' for both the MSI and coding-sequence methods. It was registered 2024-11-06 and the lab's last annual review was 2025-11-12. This is consistent with Tempus job postings listing both 6000 and X, but it is a declared field.
items.why_new: Not in the known list; it is a filing-like lab declaration that a large oncology customer's test runs on the 6000.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: The 12 'NovaSeq X' hits are few and mostly small labs, but they include Labcorp-owned Integrated Genetics/Sequenom (MaterniT NIPT) and Mass General Brigham, so some clinical conversion is declared.
items.detail: X-family records: Integrated Genetics–Sequenom (CLIA 05D2015356) MaterniT21, MaterniT GENOME and the two Genome Add-On tests, all 'Novaseq X Plus', last updated 2024-11-01. University of Michigan Molecular Genetics (CLIA 23D1088637) has BRCA1/2 (updated 2026-06-24, versions 2022-2026), TP53, CFTR, ATP7B and GDI1. MGB Laboratory for Molecular Medicine's polygenic cardiovascular risk test (registered 2025-12-04) runs on the X Plus at the Broad Clinical Laboratory. A male infertility panel (registered 2026-07-18) also names the X Plus. So a large NIPT lab has declared an X move, which matches the known NIPT-converts-first view.
items.why_new: Names the labs behind the X records and gives dates; shows NIPT already on the X and a US academic lab (Michigan) converting.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: Rival short-read platforms are almost absent from clinical test registrations: AVITI appears in 11 GTR records, all from a small Polish-linked lab, and Ultima is not detectable.
items.detail: esearch for AVITI returned 11 IDs (613429, 558563, 558561, 332665 and others). The two I opened are from the Laboratory of Human Genetics (testing at Genomed S.A., Warsaw): retinal dystrophy panel (registered 2024-10-25) and childhood absence epilepsy panel (updated 2025-01-31). Against 130 for the 6000, that is 11 AVITI records per 130 6000 records (~8%) and all from one lab family. An 'Ultima Genomics' query returned 31,252 results, so it was a loose match and gave no usable count. Clinical labs are not yet declaring rival platforms, which weakens near-term large-account leverage in the clinical book.
items.why_new: Quantifies the rival footprint in clinical test registrations. It cuts against 1B/2B in the clinical channel.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Newly registered tests are still being filed on the NovaSeq 6000 in 2026, with one registered 7 Oct 2026.
items.detail: A Dystonia Gene Panel (record 619920, Clinical Biochemical Genetics Diagnostic Laboratory) names 'Illumina Novaseq 6000' and was registered 2026-10-07. Another 6000 record (CMS mutation detection, 613591) was registered 2025-01-14 and reviewed 2026-04-20. Labs setting up new test listings in late 2026 still choose the 6000, which fits a tail that does not convert on a fixed schedule.
items.why_new: Shows a brand-new 2026 registration naming the 6000. It is one small lab, so low weight.

notes: Full lab-by-instrument tables not built: esummary XML was too large (700K characters) for the fetch tool, and I could not run Python. Remaining: (a) counts for NovaSeq 6000 AND each of Natera, Labcorp, Quest, Caris, Foundation, Guardant, Ambry, Invitae, Baylor; (b) 'NovaSeq 6000Dx' and 'NovaSeqX' queries; (c) per-record Methodology > Instrument and last-updated dates for the 26 non-Mayo 6000 records, to compute the share updated in 2025-26. Note GTR 'Instrument' can be free text, so it may not match the lab's actual fleet. The 'Ultima' term is not usable as a loose match.
